records.literal_gloss: And reigned David over all Israel, and was doing justice and righteousness for all his people.

en.L: And David reigned over all Israel, and he was doing justice and righteousness for all his people.
en.B: So David reigned over all Israel, and he did what was just and right for all his people.
en.R: David ruled over all Israel. He was fair to all his people and did what was right for them.

es.L: Y reinó David sobre todo Israel, y hacía juicio y justicia a todo su pueblo.
es.B: Así reinó David sobre todo Israel, y hacía lo que era justo y recto con todo su pueblo.
es.R: David gobernó sobre todo Israel. Era justo con todo su pueblo y hacía lo que era correcto con ellos.

fr.L: Et David régna sur tout Israël, et il pratiquait le droit et la justice pour tout son peuple.
fr.B: David régna donc sur tout Israël, et il faisait ce qui était juste et droit pour tout son peuple.
fr.R: David a régné sur tout Israël. Il était juste envers tout son peuple et il faisait ce qui était bien pour eux.

sw.L: Daudi akatawala juu ya Israeli wote, naye alikuwa akitenda hukumu na haki kwa watu wake wote.
sw.B: Basi Daudi alitawala juu ya Israeli wote, naye akawatendea watu wake wote yaliyo ya haki na ya adili.
sw.R: Daudi alitawala Israeli wote. Aliwatendea watu wake wote kwa haki, akafanya yaliyo mema kwao.

vi.L: Đa-vít trị vì trên toàn Y-sơ-ra-ên, và ông thi hành công lý và sự công chính cho toàn dân mình.
vi.B: Vậy Đa-vít trị vì toàn Y-sơ-ra-ên, và ông làm điều công bằng và chính trực cho toàn dân mình.
vi.R: Đa-vít cai trị toàn Y-sơ-ra-ên. Ông đối xử công bằng với mọi người trong dân mình và làm điều đúng cho họ.

ko.L: 그리고 다윗이 온 이스라엘을 다스렸고, 그의 모든 백성에게 공의와 정의를 행하고 있었다.
ko.B: 이렇게 다윗은 온 이스라엘을 다스렸고, 그의 모든 백성에게 공평하고 의롭게 행했다.
ko.R: 다윗은 온 이스라엘을 다스렸다. 그는 모든 백성을 공평하게 대했고, 그들을 위해 옳은 일을 했다.

pt.L: E Davi reinou sobre todo o Israel, e praticava o juízo e a justiça para todo o seu povo.
pt.B: Assim Davi reinou sobre todo o Israel, e fazia o que era justo e direito para todo o seu povo.
pt.R: Davi governou todo o Israel. Ele era justo com todo o seu povo e fazia o que era certo para eles.

am.L: ዳዊትም በእስራኤል ሁሉ ላይ ነገሠ፤ ለሕዝቡም ሁሉ ፍትሕንና ጽድቅን ያደርግ ነበር።
am.B: ስለዚህ ዳዊት በእስራኤል ሁሉ ላይ ነገሠ፤ ለሕዝቡም ሁሉ ትክክልና ቅን የሆነውን ያደርግ ነበር።
am.R: ዳዊት በእስራኤል ሁሉ ላይ ገዛ። ሕዝቡን ሁሉ በፍትሕ ይዳኝ ነበር፤ ትክክል የሆነውንም ያደርግላቸው ነበር።

hi.L: और दाऊद ने सारे इस्राएल पर राज्य किया, और वह अपनी सारी प्रजा के लिए न्याय और धार्मिकता के काम करता रहा।
hi.B: इस प्रकार दाऊद ने सारे इस्राएल पर राज्य किया, और वह अपनी सारी प्रजा के लिए वही करता था जो न्यायपूर्ण और उचित था।
hi.R: दाऊद ने सारे इस्राएल पर राज्य किया। वह अपनी सारी प्रजा के साथ न्याय करता था और उनके लिए वही करता था जो सही था।

ru.L: И царствовал Давид над всем Израилем, и творил суд и правду всему своему народу.
ru.B: Так Давид царствовал над всем Израилем и поступал справедливо и праведно со всем своим народом.
ru.R: Давид правил всем Израилем. Он был справедлив ко всему своему народу и поступал с ними правильно.

uk.L: І царював Давид над усім Ізраїлем, і чинив суд і справедливість усьому своєму народові.
uk.B: Так Давид царював над усім Ізраїлем і чинив те, що було справедливе й праведне, для всього свого народу.
uk.R: Давид правив усім Ізраїлем. Він був справедливий до всього свого народу й чинив для них те, що правильно.

decisions.choice: the same as 2 Samuel 8:15, without the second "David"
decisions.reason: 2 Samuel 8:15 repeats David's name as the subject of "was doing"; otherwise the verse is the same.

decisions.choice: doing justice and righteousness: ruling fairly and rightly
decisions.reason: As in 2 Samuel 8:15. The pair describes the ideal king (Jeremiah 22:15; Psalm 72:1-2): fair judgments and right dealing that protects the weak.

decisions.choice: was doing: an ongoing practice
decisions.reason: The verb "was" with a participle describes the steady pattern of David's rule. The verse sums up the wars and turns to how David governed; verses 15-17 name the men who served him.

decisions.choice: what was just and right (Balanced); fair ... what was right (Readable)
decisions.reason: As in 2 Samuel 8:15: Literal keeps the two nouns; Balanced and Readable use adjectives.

decisions.choice: as 2 Samuel 8:15, without the second "Davi"
decisions.reason: 2 Samuel 8:15 in Portuguese at every level; Literal drops the repeated "Davi" before "praticava", as Chronicles does (m1).

decisions.choice: parallel 2 Samuel 8:15 copied, without the second "ዳዊትም"
decisions.reason: Chronicles does not repeat the name before "was doing".

en.B: Joab son of Zeruiah was commander of the army; Jehoshaphat son of Ahilud was recorder;
en.R: Joab son of Zeruiah was the army commander. Jehoshaphat son of Ahilud kept the royal records.

es.B: Joab hijo de Sarvia era jefe del ejército; Josafat hijo de Ahilud era cronista;
es.R: Joab, hijo de Sarvia, era el jefe del ejército. Josafat, hijo de Ahilud, llevaba los registros del reino.

fr.R: Joab, fils de Tserouya, était le chef de l’armée. Josaphat, fils d’Ahiloud, tenait les archives du royaume.

sw.L: Yoabu mwana wa Seruya [alikuwa] juu ya jeshi, na Yehoshafati mwana wa Ahiludi [alikuwa] mwandishi wa kumbukumbu,
sw.B: Yoabu mwana wa Seruya alikuwa mkuu wa jeshi; Yehoshafati mwana wa Ahiludi alikuwa mwandishi wa kumbukumbu;

decisions.choice: Abimelech son of Abiathar, where 2 Samuel 8:17 has Ahimelech son of Abiathar
decisions.reason: The two names differ by one similar letter in Hebrew, and the Greek translation of Chronicles reads Ahimelech here. Elsewhere Abiathar is the son of Ahimelech (1 Samuel 22:20), and 24:6 has "Ahimelech son of Abiathar"; see the note at 2 Samuel 8:17 on whether the names were reversed in copying or Abiathar had a son named after his grandfather. The Hebrew text is followed here.

decisions.choice: Shavsha, where 2 Samuel 8:17 has Seraiah
decisions.reason: The royal secretary is Seraiah in 2 Samuel 8:17, Sheva in 2 Samuel 20:25 and Shisha in 1 Kings 4:3. These are probably spellings of one name, perhaps a foreign one, written differently in each list.

decisions.choice: Zadok son of Ahitub: a priest of Aaron's line
decisions.reason: As in 2 Samuel 8:17. Chronicles traces him through Eleazar son of Aaron (5:34), and his family served as chief priests from Solomon's reign on.

decisions.choice: the royal secretary
decisions.reason: As in 2 Samuel 8:17: Readable adds "royal" to show this was a high office at court.

decisions.choice: Abimeleque; Sausa
decisions.reason: 2 Samuel 8:17 in Portuguese with Chronicles' two names (m1, m2): "Abimeleque", the form of Genesis 20 in Portuguese, kept as the Hebrew here has it rather than corrected to "Aimeleque", and "Sausa" for "Seraías", in its usual Brazilian form.

decisions.choice: parallel 2 Samuel 8:17 copied, with Abimelech "አቢሜሌክ" (as Judges 9) for Ahimelech "አሂሜሌክ" and Shavsha "ሻውሻ" (new) for Seraiah "ሠራያ"
decisions.reason: Chronicles spells both names differently (meaning decisions); the names follow its Hebrew.

decisions.choice: "अबीमेलेक", "शवशा"
decisions.reason: The Chronicles text has Abimelech and Shavsha, as the English does, where 2 Samuel 8:17 has Ahimelech and Seraiah; "अबीमेलेक" takes the form of Judges 9, and Shavsha is transcribed from the Hebrew.

decisions.choice: "Авимелех", "Шавша"
decisions.reason: Chronicles has other forms of the two names than 2 Samuel 8:17 (m1, m2); the Russian follows the Chronicles Hebrew in their traditional forms.

decisions.choice: David's sons were the chief officials at the king's side, where 2 Samuel 8:18 says they were priests
alternatives: the sons of David were priests (2 Samuel 8:18)
decisions.reason: 2 Samuel 8:18 says "the sons of David were priests", using the ordinary word for priest. Chronicles says instead that they were "the first at the king's hand", his highest officials. In Chronicles only the sons of Aaron serve as priests (6:34; 23:13; 2 Chronicles 26:18), so the writer describes the princes' place at court without calling them priests. This may also show how the word in Samuel was understood: as chief ministers of the king rather than men who served at the altar (see the note at 2 Samuel 8:18).

decisions.choice: the first at the king's hand: the highest officials, next to the king
decisions.reason: "First" means foremost in rank, and "at the hand of" means at his side, close to him. The princes held the places of greatest honor and trust at court.

decisions.choice: Cherethites and Pelethites: foreign soldiers who formed the king's guard
decisions.reason: As in 2 Samuel 8:18: soldiers from the Philistine coast who served as David's personal guard (2 Samuel 15:18; 1 Kings 1:38). Here the Hebrew says Benaiah was "over" them, which 2 Samuel 8:18 leaves unsaid.

decisions.choice: the chief officials at the king's side (Balanced); the king's chief officials, serving at his side (Readable)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "the first ones"; Balanced and Readable say what being first at the king's side meant. Readable also says who the Cherethites and Pelethites were, as in 2 Samuel 8:18.

decisions.choice: os primeiros ao lado do rei (L); os principais oficiais (B, R)
decisions.reason: 2 Samuel 8:18 in Portuguese for Benaia and the guard ("comandava" at Balanced, "o chefe ... guarda pessoal do rei" at Readable), with Chronicles' "over" bracketed at Literal as "[estava] sobre". Where Samuel says David's sons "eram sacerdotes", Chronicles has "the first at the king's hand" (m1, m2): Literal says "os primeiros ao lado do rei", since "à mão do rei" is not Portuguese for being at someone's side, and Balanced and Readable say "os principais oficiais".

decisions.choice: parallel 2 Samuel 8:18: Benaiah "over" the Cherethites and Pelethites ("በከሪታውያንና በፈሊታውያን ላይ", as Samuel's Balanced); David's sons "the first at the king's side" for Samuel's "priests"
decisions.reason: Chronicles has "over" where the Hebrew of Samuel has "and", and calls David's sons the chief officials beside the king, not priests (meaning decision).

decisions.reason: Where 2 Samuel 8:18 calls David's sons priests, Chronicles calls them "the first at the king's side"; the Hindi follows the Chronicles Hebrew, with Literal keeping "first" and the other levels saying what it meant.

decisions.reason: 2 Samuel 8:18 says David's sons were priests; Chronicles says they were the first at the king's side (m1, m2), so the wording differs there.
